question: An imaginary line or a line on a map or chart joining all the points having the same depth below the water surface such as sea water is called _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __isobaths__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Isobath____​__

 __
 
• Isobath is an imaginary line or a line on a map or chart that connects all points having the same depth below a water surface (as of an ocean, sea, or lake).
 
• Isobaths** are a type of isopleth line. **
 
• Isobaths **can also be used to indicate the depth of an aquifer or water table below the earth's surface. **
 
• The word isobath comes from the Greek words is- and bathos, which mean "depth".
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Isopleths
 Description
 
 

 Isotherm
 
 
 
• An isotherm is a line drawn on a map or chart joining points with the same temperature.
 
• Isotherms are commonly used in meteorology to show the distribution of temperature at the Earth's surface. 
 
• Isotherms are commonly used in meteorology to view temperature distribution on the surface of the Earth or a chart showing steady or constant pressure
 
 
 
 

 Isobar
 
 
 
• Isobar, line on a weather map of constant line of barometric pressure drawn on a given reference surface. 
 
• The isobaric pattern on a constant-height surface is extremely useful in weather forecasting because of the close association between pressure and weather.
 
 
 
 

 Isohyet
 
 
 
• An isohyet is a line on a map that connects points that have the same amounts of precipitation in a given period or for a particular storm. a line on a map that connects places that have the same amount of rain.
 
 
 
 

 Isonomic
 
 
 
• A line on a chart connecting points of equal abundance values of a plant species sampled in different sections of an area.
 
• Isonomes of different species from the same area are compared in studies of plant distribution.
 
 
 
 

 Isohypse
 
 
 
• A line on a map connecting points of equal height.
 
 
 
 

 Isohel
 
 
 
• a line is drawn on a map or chart connecting places of equal duration of sunshine
 
 
 
 

 Isochron
 
 
 
• An imaginary line or a line on a chart connecting points at which an event occurs simultaneously or which represents the same time or time difference.
